Variants.Content: The Summer Sea stretches between southern Westeros and the southern coast of Essos, its sea lanes reaching Dorne, the Stepstones, Lys, Volantis, Slaver's Bay, and the Summer Isles. These warm waters nurture trade in spices, wine, hardwoods, silk, and slaves, while drawing pirates, privateers, and fleets contending for ports. Seasonal winds govern the timing of long voyages, while fresh water, canvas, salt provisions, and reliable pilots decide whether a ship arrives. At noble feasts it appears as exotic wares, while on the bodies of sailors it shows as sun-cracked skin, fevers, and the exhaustion of months out of sight of land.

Those who know the Summer Sea arrange their fortunes by the seasons of the wind. Sailing a few days early may fetch a handsome price, while misjudging a gale can send a whole cargo of spices and years of savings to the bottom.

Coastal rulers collect taxes from the sea, yet must also guard against pirates and slavers. If a port has tollgates but no patrol ships, the customs officers will grow rich while the coastal villages grow ever emptier.

Common folk draw salt, work, and foreign goods from the Summer Sea, and may also have their kin carried off by it. To those chained in a ship's hold, these warm waters are not a road, but a wall without a door.
